# Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) Research Note

## Snapshot

**Company:** Johnson & Johnson  
**Ticker:** JNJ  
**Current Price:** $227.19 USD  
**Market Cap:** $546.9 billion  
**P/E Ratio:** 26.33 (Yahoo Finance); 18.81 (FMP trailing)  
**52-Week Range:** $146.12 – $251.71  
**1-Month Price Change:** -6.52%  
**Sector:** Healthcare – Drug Manufacturers (Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices)  

[Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]

**Macro Context:**  
JNJ operates in a moderating rate environment with the Federal Funds Rate at 3.64% (falling trend) as of April 2026, supporting equity valuations in large-cap healthcare. CPI stands at 330.29 (rising trend), indicating persistent inflation pressures. The 10Y-2Y Treasury spread is positive at 0.51 bps (falling), suggesting limited immediate recession risk. The S&P 500 is at 7,230.12 (rising trend), reflecting broader market strength. Unemployment has ticked up to 4.3% (rising trend), signaling a softening labor market.  

[Source: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)]

---

## Bull Case

1. **Strong Q1 2026 earnings beat with raised guidance:** JNJ reported Q1 2026 results that exceeded analyst estimates and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $100.3B–$101.3B (midpoint $100.8B, up from $100.5B previously). Adjusted EPS guidance was lifted to $11.45–$11.65 (midpoint $11.55 vs. $11.53 prior). Operational sales growth of 11.5% in Q4 2025 demonstrates momentum despite headwinds.  
[Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/sectors/healthcare/articles/johnson-johnson-raises-2026-outlook-114019247.html]  
[Source: https://www.investor.jnj.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Johnson--Johnson-reports-Q1-2026-results-raises-2026-outlook/default.aspx]

2. **Blockbuster growth drivers offsetting Stelara decline:** Darzalex (multiple myeloma) is surging and positioned to become one of JNJ's largest products, with strong double-digit growth. Tremfya (immunology) grew 40% to approximately $5.2 billion in 2025 and is expanding into Stelara's former indications. Carvykti (CAR-T therapy) nearly doubled sales to $1.9 billion in 2025, crossing the blockbuster threshold. Spravato (depression/neuroscience) increased sales 57% to $1.7 billion in 2025. Erleada (prostate cancer) grew 19% to $3.6 billion. These products collectively provide a robust growth engine post-Stelara.  
[Source: https://www.fiercepharma.com/pharma/led-darzalex-surge-jj-expects-revenue-reach-100b-2026]  
[Source: https://www.labiotech.eu/in-depth/jj-pipeline/]

3. **Successful strategic transformation into pure-play pharma/medtech:** The 2023 spin-off of Kenvue (consumer health) has streamlined JNJ into a focused Innovative Medicine and MedTech company, eliminating lower-margin consumer products and allowing management to concentrate capital and R&D on higher-growth, higher-margin therapeutic areas (oncology, immunology, neuroscience) and medical devices. This strategic repositioning has improved operating margins (27.2% as of FMP data) and positioning for future growth.  
[Source: https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/finterra-2026-4-14-the-new-j-and-j-a-2026-deep-dive-into-the-global-healthcare-titan]  
[Source: https://investors.kenvue.com/financial-news/news-details/2023/Kenvue-Becomes-a-Fully-Independent-Company-Following-Final-Separation-from-Johnson--Johnson/default.aspx]

4. **Strong balance sheet and dividend profile:** JNJ maintains a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.59, indicating conservative leverage. The company is consistently cited as a top dividend stock with a long track record of dividend growth, providing downside protection and income appeal for institutional investors.  
[Source: Financial Modeling Prep]  
[Source: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2913259/why-johnson-johnson-jnj-is-a-top-dividend-stock-for-your-portfolio?cid=CS-STOCKNEWSAPI-FT-tale_of_the_tape|yseop_template_5-2913259]

5. **Psychedelic medicine leadership:** JNJ's Spravato (esketamine) represents a $1.7 billion franchise in psychedelic-derived medicine for treatment-resistant depression, positioning the company at the forefront of a nascent therapeutic category with significant long-term growth potential as mental health treatment paradigms evolve.  
[Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0nvPZ1ilFhE]

---

## Bear Case

1. **Stelara patent cliff creating immediate revenue headwinds:** Stelara, which peaked at $11 billion in 2023, lost U.S. patent exclusivity in 2025 and faces full biosimilar competition in 2026. This represents the first full year of material revenue decline from what was once the backbone of JNJ's immunology franchise. Q1 2026 results showed Stelara sales plunging, and despite newer products like Tremfya, the revenue hole is substantial and embedded in current numbers.  
[Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/14/johnson-and-johnson-jnj-earnings-q1-2026.html]  
[Source: https://www.labiotech.eu/in-depth/jj-pipeline/]  
[Source: https://www.investing.com/analysis/johnson--johnson-clears-the-patent-cliff-as-2026-guidance-resets-the-narrative-200673620]

2. **Massive ongoing talc litigation liability:** JNJ faces 67,376 lawsuits in the talcum powder multidistrict litigation (MDL 2738) as of April 2026. The company has attempted three bankruptcy settlements (proposing $2B in 2021, $8.9B in 2023, and $6.48B in 2024), but none have been approved. Recent verdicts include a $1.5 billion judgment in December 2025 and a $15 million Connecticut verdict in early 2026. Bloomberg Intelligence suggests ultimate settlement costs could reach $11 billion. The U.S. Trustee has accused JNJ of "forum shopping" in bankruptcy proceedings, and litigation continues to generate headline risk and uncertainty.  
[Source: https://www.drugwatch.com/talcum-powder/settlements/]  
[Source: https://www.darrow.ai/resources/johnson-and-johnson-talc-lawsuit]  
[Source: https://trulaw.com/johnson-and-johnson-talcum-powder-lawsuit/]

3. **Price multiple compression and valuation concerns:** The stock has declined 6.52% over the past month, underperforming the rising S&P 500 (up to 7,230 level). At a trailing P/E of 18.8 (FMP) to 26.3 (Yahoo Finance), JNJ trades at a premium to historical norms given patent cliff headwinds and litigation overhang. The stock is trading well below its 52-week high of $251.71, reflecting investor skepticism about whether guidance raises are sufficient.  
[Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]  
[Source: Financial Modeling Prep]

4. **Regulatory and pricing pressure:** Despite signing Trump administration drug pricing deals, JNJ was among 16 companies that still raised prices on 872 brand-name drugs in early January 2026, with a median increase of 4%. This creates reputational and regulatory risk in an environment of heightened scrutiny on pharmaceutical pricing, potentially limiting future pricing power.  
[Source: https://www.investing.com/analysis/johnson--johnson-clears-the-patent-cliff-as-2026-guidance-resets-the-narrative-200673620]

5. **Execution risk on pipeline and biosimilar competition:** While Darzalex, Tremfya, and Carvykti are growing rapidly, they face competitive pressures in crowded oncology and immunology markets. The company's ability to achieve its stated goal of becoming the #1 oncology player by 2030 depends on flawless execution across multiple assets, regulatory approvals, and market share gains against entrenched competitors like Merck (Keytruda) and Bristol Myers Squibb (Opdivo).  
[Source: https://www.syneticx.com/blog/jnj.html]

---

## Recent Catalysts

1. **Q1 2026 earnings beat and guidance raise (April 14, 2026):** JNJ reported better-than-expected Q1 2026 results and raised full-year guidance, beating Wall Street estimates. Innovative Medicine operational sales grew 7.4%, driven by Darzalex, Carvykti, Tremfya, and Spravato. The raise was viewed as conservative by some analysts, setting up potential for further upside.  
[Source: https://www.investor.jnj.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Johnson--Johnson-reports-Q1-2026-results-raises-2026-outlook/default.aspx]  
[Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/johnson-johnson-jnj-exceeds-first-185244037.html]

2. **Appointment of new VP of Investor Relations (April 30, 2026):** JNJ appointed Ryan Koors as Vice President, Investor Relations, signaling a refresh in investor communication as the company navigates its post-Kenvue, post-Stelara transformation.  
[Source: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260430443361/en/Johnson-Johnson-Appoints-Ryan-Koors-as-Vice-President-Investor-Relations/]

3. **Most recent 10-Q filing (April 22, 2026):** JNJ filed its Q1 2026 10-Q on April 22, 2026, providing detailed financial results for the quarter ending March 29, 2026.  
[Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/200406/000020040626000087/jnj-20260329.htm]

4. **8-K filing (April 28, 2026):** JNJ filed an 8-K on April 28, 2026, likely related to material corporate events or updates following the Q1 earnings release.  
[Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/200406/000020040626000089/jnj-20260423.htm]

5. **Ongoing talc bankruptcy proceedings:** JNJ's subsidiary Red River Talc remains in bankruptcy proceedings attempting to resolve talc litigation. As of March 2026, the third bankruptcy attempt collapsed, and litigation resumed in federal and state courts. The U.S. Trustee accused the company of forum shopping by attempting to move the case from Texas to New Jersey. Settlement negotiations remain fluid.  
[Source: https://lawfold.com/johnson-and-johnson-talc-lawsuit/]  
[Source: https://trulaw.com/johnson-and-johnson-talcum-powder-lawsuit/]

## Risks

**Macro Risks:**
- **Rising inflation:** CPI is on a rising trend (330.29 as of March 2026), which could pressure input costs, labor expenses, and squeeze margins despite JNJ's pricing power. [Source: FRED]
- **Softening labor market:** Unemployment rising to 4.3% signals potential economic deceleration, which could reduce elective medical procedure volumes in MedTech and impact pharmaceutical demand. [Source: FRED]
- **Interest rate volatility:** While the Fed Funds rate is falling (3.64%), the narrowing 10Y-2Y spread (0.51 bps, falling) suggests potential for yield curve inversion recurrence, which could pressure valuations and financing costs. [Source: FRED]

**Company-Specific Risks:**
- **Talc litigation overhang:** With 67,376 active lawsuits and no approved settlement despite three bankruptcy attempts, JNJ faces ongoing headline risk, unpredictable verdict outcomes (including recent multi-billion-dollar judgments), and potential for $11 billion+ in ultimate settlement costs. [Source: Drugwatch; Darrow.ai]
- **Stelara revenue cliff:** Full-year 2026 represents the first year of complete biosimilar erosion for an $11 billion peak product. Even with Tremfya's 40% growth, the pace of replacement remains uncertain. [Source: Labiotech; CNBC]
- **Pipeline execution risk:** JNJ's growth thesis depends on multiple products (Darzalex, Carvykti, Tremfya, Spravato) sustaining double-digit growth rates in highly competitive therapeutic areas. Any regulatory setbacks, clinical trial failures, or competitive losses could derail the bull case. [Source: SyneticX]
- **Regulatory pricing pressure:** Despite pricing deal rhetoric, JNJ raised prices 4% on multiple drugs in January 2026, creating regulatory and political risk in a contentious drug pricing environment. [Source: Investing.com]

---

## What to Watch Next

1. **Next Earnings Date: July 15, 2026:** JNJ will report Q2 2026 results. Key metrics to monitor include: (a) Darzalex revenue growth trajectory and market share in multiple myeloma, (b) Tremfya's ability to offset Stelara declines, (c) MedTech segment growth (particularly Vision and Surgery), and (d) any updates on talc litigation settlement progress or additional adverse verdicts. [Source: Financial Modeling Prep]

2. **Talc bankruptcy resolution:** The outcome of the Red River Talc bankruptcy proceedings in 2026 will determine whether JNJ achieves a global settlement or faces continued jury trials and headline risk. Monitor court filings in the U.S. District Court for New Jersey (MDL 2738) for settlement approval or case dismissal. [Source: Drugwatch; Trulaw]

3. **Full-year guidance updates and Stelara erosion pace:** Watch for JNJ's full-year guidance updates in Q2 and Q3 earnings. If biosimilar erosion of Stelara is slower than feared or if Tremfya/Darzalex growth accelerates beyond expectations, the stock could re-rate higher. Conversely, if Stelara declines faster than modeled, guidance could be at risk despite Q1 raise. [Source: Labiotech; FiercePharma]
